subject: EdgeLabs vendor evaluation — capacity, benchmarks, and renewal timeline
messages:
From: Anna Lee <anna.lee@edgelabs.ai>
To: dylan.brooks@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@edgelabs.ai
Date: Thu, 25 Jun 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: EdgeLabs vendor evaluation & Q3 renewal capacity questions

Hi Dylan,

Quick note from the vendor review side — procurement is pushing us to evaluate CloudScale for next quarter. They claim a 20% unit-cost savings and are promising reserved burst capacity for our peak windows. That, plus a bundled observation layer, is making execs nervous.

We have a renewal coming up Aug 1 and are planning a short bake-off benchmarking latency and concurrency for our peak inference patterns (45-90s sequences, KV cache heavy). We'd like to include Redwood in the formal comparison.

Can you:
- Confirm what dedicated capacity options look like for +30% concurrent throughput (short-term)?
- Share a lightweight benchmark plan we can run (scripts, metrics to collect)?
- Tell me what short-term commercial flexibility is possible if we need committed capacity?

Procurement timeline: decision window 2–3 weeks.

Thanks — Anna
Anna Lee
Head of Platform
EdgeLabs

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Lee <anna.lee@edgelabs.ai>
Cc: monica.patel@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 26 Jun 2026 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: EdgeLabs vendor evaluation & Q3 renewal capacity questions

Anna — thanks for the heads up and for looping us in early. We take competitive evaluations seriously and want to make this as low-friction as possible. High-level responses:

- Dedicated capacity: we can provision a temporary Dedicated pool sized for +30% concurrency for a 30–60 day test window. We can scope it to your peak region and pin model variants to eliminate cold-start variability.
- Benchmark plan: attaching a short harness (benchmark_harness_instructions.xlsx) and a one-page proposal (EdgeLabs_proposal_v3.pdf). The harness includes a reproducible load pattern, expected metrics (p50/p95 latency, tail variance, tokens/sec, token cost) and suggested KV cache settings.
- Commercial flexibility: I can offer a limited short-term credit and a one-time committed-rate hold for customers who convert the test into a Dedicated contract within 14 days of sign-off. I'll escalate approvals if you need larger credits.

Proposed next steps:
1) If procurement agrees, we set up a 2-hour kickoff next week with Monica (solutions) to validate test harness and the model variants you'll run.
2) We provision a Dedicated test pool and a Datadog dashboard for the run.
3) Run a 48-hour steady-state and a 6-hour peak simulation, then compare logs/metrics.

Attachments: benchmark_harness_instructions.xlsx; EdgeLabs_proposal_v3.pdf

If procurement wants SOC2 artifacts or an SLA exception, say the word and I'll bring in our security and revenue ops teams.

—Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Lee <anna.lee@edgelabs.ai>, dylan.brooks@redwood.ai
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 29 Jun 2026 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: EdgeLabs vendor evaluation & Q3 renewal capacity questions

Anna / Dylan — Monica here (solutions eng). Quick technical notes for the run and items to watch: 

- Test harness: the attached workbook has the load script and a small Docker image we recommend for controlled clients. Use the "kv-heavy" profile for the sequences you mentioned.
- Metrics to capture: p50/p95/p99 latency, per-request token counts, KV cache hit ratio, GPU utilization, and end-to-end tail latency under concurrent warm connections. We'll provide a Datadog dashboard template you can install.
- Model parity: please confirm the exact model versions & tokenizer configs you plan to use. Differences in tokenization give noisy cost comparisons.
- Failure modes: CloudScale's preemptible nodes can look cheaper on paper but cause tail spikes under cold starts. We'll instrument to capture spike counts and recovery time.

I can host the kickoff Tuesday 6/30 10:00–12:00 PT or Wed 7/1 14:00–16:00 PT. Which works?

Attachments: benchmark_harness_instructions.xlsx (test scripts). Dashboard: https://app.datadog.com/edge/boards/edgelabs-inference-run

—Monica
Monica Patel
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Anna Lee <anna.lee@edgelabs.ai>
To: dylan.brooks@redwood.ai, monica.patel@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@edgelabs.ai
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2026 08:01:00 -0700
Subject: Re: EdgeLabs vendor evaluation & Q3 renewal capacity questions

Thanks both — Tue 6/30 10:00 PT works for us. I'll loop in Procurement (copied). A few notes from procurement and C-suite: 

- Procurement wants an SLA exception form and confirmation of audit artifacts (SOC2 report, data retention policy) before they greenlight a hands-on test.
- C-suite is asking for hard numbers: if Redwood can provide cost per 1M tokens at our peak profile and a committed capacity price for a 12-month term, that would be persuasive.
- Timeline is tight — procurement decision in ~10 business days.

Can someone confirm you can share SOC2 and the SLA exception doc by EOD Monday 7/6? Procurement won't delay the review without them.

Best,
Anna
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Lee <anna.lee@edgelabs.ai>, dylan.brooks@redwood.ai
Cc: monica.patel@redwood.ai, procurement@edgelabs.ai
Date: Fri, 03 Jul 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: EdgeLabs vendor evaluation & Q3 renewal capacity questions

Anna — Rishi here (Sales Lead). Appreciate the clarity and timeline. I reviewed the ask with Rev Ops and Security. Quick concrete commitments from Redwood to keep EdgeLabs in the running: 

- We will provide SOC2 Type II report and our data retention policy by EOD Monday 7/6.
- We're approving a limited SLA exception for this test window (details attached: SLA-exception-request.pdf). The exception covers pinned capacity and an elevated incident response SLA for the 30–60 day test.
- Commercial concession: a one-time credit equal to 10% of the estimated monthly committed spend if you sign an annual Dedicated contract within 14 days of test close. Larger credits considered for expanded committed capacity; we can run the numbers in the deal doc.

Next steps:
- Dylan to send a final signed DocuSign proposal for the dedicated test (link below) — sign & return to provision capacity.
- Monica will run the kickoff and share the dashboard + harness.
- Procurement: please confirm the legal contact to review the SLA exception and any redlines.

DocuSign: https://app.docusign.com/REDW/edge-2026-proposal
Attachments: SLA-exception-request.pdf

Looking forward to the kickoff next week.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
